# FDG2027

> DO provide strongly typed APIs if at all possible.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 2.2.3.3 Strong Typing.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Not an analyzer candidate: object, string or property-bag parameters are sometimes required (the body allows property bags), so a check would have to guess intent.

## From the book

Do not rely exclusively on weakly typed APIs such as property bags. In cases in which a property bag is required, provide strongly typed properties for the most common properties in the bag.

> **Vance Morrison:** The strong typing (and thus much better Intelli-Sense) is a crucial reason why .NET frameworks are easier to “learn by programming” than your typical COM API. From time to time, I still need to use functionality exposed through COM, and as long as it stays strongly typed, I do fine. But all too often APIs return or take a generic object or string parameter or passed DWORD when an enumeration is needed, and it takes me ten times longer to discover what exactly needs to be passed.
